name: Jeddah
notes: Most existing submarine cables serving Saudi Arabia land at Jeddah, on the Red Sea coast, for onward connectivity to Egypt and Europe. center3 alone operates landing stations across three separate Jeddah buildings.
source_name: Submarine Cable Map -- Jeddah, Saudi Arabia landing point

name: Doha
cable_systems: AAE-1; FALCON; Fiber Optic Gulf (FOG); GBI; Qatar-UAE; TGN-Gulf
notes: Doha Cable Landing Station is Qatar's primary Red Sea/Gulf cable gateway; Qatar also has a secondary Ooredoo landing station at Halul.
source_name: Submarine Networks -- Qatar cable landing stations

name: Fujairah
cable_systems: AAE-1; BBG; FLAG Europe-Asia (FEA); IMEWE; SMW3; SMW4; TEAMS; TGN
notes: Fujairah is ranked the biggest single location for landing submarine cables in the Middle East -- notable because it sits on the Gulf of Oman coast, outside the Strait of Hormuz, giving it a direct Indian Ocean route that bypasses Hormuz entirely.
source_name: Submarine Networks -- Etisalat Fujairah Cable Landing Station
